question: A 26-year-old man is brought to the primary health centre by his family. He believes his thoughts are being broadcast to others, hears voices commenting on his actions, has stopped bathing, and sits motionless for hours. Which of the following symptom groupings correctly classifies his features?

answers.text: Thought broadcast and auditory hallucinations are negative symptoms; social withdrawal and avolition are positive symptoms.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. This reverses the classification. Thought broadcast (a passivity phenomenon) and auditory hallucinations are positive symptoms; social withdrawal and avolition are negative symptoms.

answers.text: Thought broadcast and auditory hallucinations are positive symptoms; social withdrawal and avolition are negative symptoms.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Positive symptoms (added experiences — delusions, hallucinations, passivity phenomena such as thought broadcast) are distinct from negative symptoms (diminished function — avolition, alogia, affective blunting, social withdrawal).

answers.text: All four features — thought broadcast, hallucinations, withdrawal, and avolition — are positive symptoms of schizophrenia.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Negative symptoms represent a loss or reduction of normal function. Avolition and social withdrawal are negative symptoms, not positive ones.

answers.text: Thought broadcast is a cognitive symptom; auditory hallucinations are a positive symptom; withdrawal and avolition are both disorganised symptoms.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Thought broadcast is a passivity phenomenon classified under positive symptoms. Avolition and social withdrawal are negative symptoms, not disorganised symptoms.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the two-domain model of schizophrenia symptoms. Positive symptoms add experiences (delusions, hallucinations, passivity); negative symptoms subtract function (avolition, alogia, flat affect, social withdrawal).
Well done. Correctly separating positive (productive) from negative (deficit) symptoms is essential for formulating a diagnosis and choosing treatment in ICD-11 and DSM-5.
